info.title: National Auto Spares — Billing & Inventory API

post.description:
Open a session with no password, when this server is configured to allow it.

The shop runs from one computer and wanted the application to open straight into
billing. This is how: the browser asks for a session, and a server that has been told
to vouch for it issues an ordinary one.

**Disabled unless somebody turns it on.** `BM_UNATTENDED_ACCESS` is off by default and
a server with it off refuses here, so no deployment acquires this by upgrading. When
it is on, `BM_UNATTENDED_USERNAME` names the account the session belongs to — the
audit trail still says who acted, and the row carries a reason recording that no
password was presented.

**Nothing downstream changes.** The response is the same `SessionOut` a login returns,
with the same access token, the same rotating refresh cookie, the same permissions and
the same device registration. Every other endpoint still demands that token and still
checks its permissions; a revoked device is still refused here and everywhere else.

**The risk, stated plainly:** anyone who can reach this endpoint gets a working
session. Enable it only where the network is already controlled — bound to localhost,
or on a LAN the shop owns — never on a server reachable from the open internet.

Rotates the token. Presenting a consumed one revokes the whole family
(FR-AUTH-002) — a consumed token in the wild means the cookie was copied.

get.description: The caller's own context. Needs no specific permission.

post.description:

Seed the default units for a business created after migration 0016 ran.

Units are reference data a spare-parts shop cannot operate without. A tax rate, a
product or a business identity is **never** seeded.

Response List Brands Api V1 Brands Get
Response List Categories Api V1 Categories Get
Response List Balances Api V1 Inventory Balances Get

get.description:
The append-only ledger (FR-INV-001) — one product's complete history.

Every movement is here, not only sales: the opening figure, each sheet arrival, each
correction, each sale, and each reversal of a cancelled bill. `balance_after` is the
stock the database actually held after that row, recorded when the movement was
written — so the history is read from the ledger and never reconstructed backwards
from today's total.

`oldest_first=true` is what the History panel asks for, so the running balance reads
downwards.

schema.title: Response List Movements Api V1 Inventory Movements Get

get.description:
What moved in or out of stock over a business-local date range (the Stock Report).

The per-product History answers "what happened to this part"; this answers "what
happened in this period", from the same append-only ledger — so the two can never
disagree and nothing is recomputed from the current total. `end_date` defaults to
`on_date`, so a single day's report (the original shape of this endpoint) is just the
range where both ends are the same day.

`kind=added` is every movement that **increased** stock: the opening figure, a
purchase receipt, the owner's stock sheet, a correction upwards, a customer return, an
applied import, and the reversal of a cancelled bill. `kind=sold` is `reason = 'sale'`
alone — what customers took away. `kind=adjusted` is every other decrease — a
correction downwards, scrap, a transfer out, a supplier return — the movements that
belonged to neither bucket before this existed.

Three exclusions are structural rather than filtered, which is what makes them
reliable: a **draft** writes no movement, a **reprint** writes no movement, and a
**credit payment** moves money rather than goods. None of them can appear here
whatever this endpoint does.

`stock_before` and `stock_after` are the ledger's own figures. The day boundary is the
business-local one (`(created_at AT TIME ZONE …)::date`), the same boundary Daily
Bills uses, so the two screens agree on what "today" means.

parameters.name: end_date

schema.description: Business-local end date, inclusive. Defaults to on_date.
schema.title: End Date

parameters.description: Business-local end date, inclusive. Defaults to on_date.

schema.title: Response Movement Report Api V1 Inventory Movements Report Get

get.description:
What would saving this item name do — add a new product, or top up an existing one?

Read-only, and answered by the **same** matcher the save uses, so the screen's
"will update existing stock" can never promise something the save then does
differently (FR-INV-008, the owner's stock sheet).

schema.title: Response Resolve Stock Entry Api V1 Inventory Stock Entries Resolve Get

post.description:
Save a sheet of stock arrivals. **Adds to stock; never replaces it.**

The route declares `catalog.write` because a row may create a product;
`StockEntryService` additionally re-asserts `inventory.adjust`, so a caller who may
edit the catalog but not move stock is refused there rather than here.

The key is **claimed**, not merely required. Requiring the header and then ignoring it
is worse than not asking for it: the caller is told the retry is safe while a second
press books the delivery a second time, and because `stock_movements` can never be
deleted the only correction left is a third, opposite movement. `claim` runs before
any stock is locked and `store_response` commits in the same transaction as the
movements, so a replay returns the first outcome verbatim (`§5.2.1`, `§5.2.8`).

schema.title: Response Create Stock Entries Api V1 Inventory Stock Entries Post

post.description:
A reasoned, audited correction. `Idempotency-Key` is required so a retried
adjustment cannot be applied twice.

schema.title: Response Create Adjustment Api V1 Inventory Adjustments Post

get.description:
Read-only. **Reports and never repairs** (FR-INV-006).

Also carries T3-04's numbering check: per series, `max(sequence_number) + 1` must
equal `next_number`. A mismatch indicates a lost update and is reported, not
corrected.

schema.title: Response Latest Reconciliation Api V1 Inventory Reconciliation Latest Get

post.description:
Runs the check now rather than waiting for the nightly job.

Still read-only with respect to balances — it writes only its own report row.

post.description:
Start a physical stock count for the caller's branch (Feature A.6).

Refuses with `STOCK_COUNT_ALREADY_OPEN` if one is already open — two concurrent
counts of the same shelf is how a count gets applied twice.

Every product with a balance in the branch, counted or not, with the
**current** system quantity and the discrepancy (`null` until counted).

Response Cancel Stock Count Api V1 Inventory Stock Counts  Session Id  Cancel Post

get.description:
The customer directory, newest first.

Added because there was no way to list customers at all. `GET /customers/search`
needs a term, and the only other read-many is `GET /credit/customers`, which
inner-joins credit invoices — it answers "who owes us money" and is the top of the
Credit Bills view. The Customers screen was reading from it, so a customer with no
credit invoice could not be seen or found there, and one created through
`Add a customer` appeared to vanish.

Declared before `/{customer_id}` because FastAPI matches in declaration order and
`""` would otherwise be swallowed by the path-parameter route.

`cursor` is opaque: the previous page's last `created_at` as epoch microseconds.
Deliberately **not** ISO-8601 — an ISO timestamp with an offset contains a `+`, which
a query string decodes as a space, so a caller who pasted `next_cursor` straight into
a URL got a 422. Microseconds match PostgreSQL's `timestamptz` precision, sort as an
integer, and need no escaping.

Keyset, not offset: a directory that grows while someone pages through it must not
skip or repeat a row.

Suggestions for the billing screen.

**`query` is optional on purpose.** The field is focused before anything is typed,
and the recently-used list is the most useful thing to show at that moment.

post.description:
Get-or-create by normalised name, and mark it used.

`200`, not `201`: the common outcome is "this mechanic already existed", and a
status code that claims a creation every time would be a lie the client then has to
ignore. `created` in the body carries the truth.

Response Get Draft Api V1 Drafts  Draft Id  Get

put.description:
Saving a draft **never** finalises a sale and **never** deducts stock
(FR-DRAFT-005).

schema.title: Response Upsert Draft Api V1 Drafts  Draft Id  Put

delete.description:
`Clear Draft`. Marks `cancelled`, audited, **never** hard-deletes and never
removes a finalised sale.

schema.title: Response Takeover Draft Api V1 Drafts  Draft Id  Takeover Post

post.description:
Atomically finalise a cash or credit sale.

Everything between BEGIN and COMMIT either all happens or none of it does
(FR-SALE-001): the invoice, its item snapshots, the stock movements, any payment, the
draft's finalised state, the audit row and the outbox event. Stock is deducted
**exactly once**.

schema.title: Response Finalize Sale Api V1 Sales Finalize Post

post.description:
Writes payment and allocation rows **only**.

`Idempotency-Key` is required (FR-PAY-004), so a retried submission records one
payment rather than two.

schema.title: Response Record Payment Api V1 Payments Post
Response List Payments Api V1 Payments Get

post.description: Creates a reversal row. The original is **never** edited (FR-PAY-005).

schema.title: Response Reverse Payment Api V1 Payments  Payment Id  Reverse Post

get.description: Derived from authoritative data (FR-CREDIT-002), never from a cache table.

schema.title: Response Credit Outstanding Api V1 Credit Outstanding Get
Response Ageing Summary Api V1 Credit Ageing Summary Get

get.description:
The top level of the Credit Bills view (FR-CREDIT-011, FR-RPT-028).

Every aggregate is **server-computed** — the client never sums these as
authoritative (FR-RPT-030, ADR-032). Grouping keys on `customer_id`, so a rename
changes only the label (FR-RPT-029).

schema.title: Response Credit Customers Api V1 Credit Customers Get

post.description: Owner-only. Produces a credit note carrying the reason.

schema.title: Response Write Off Api V1 Credit Write Off Post
Response Allocate Credit Note Api V1 Credit Notes  Note Id  Allocations Post

get.description:
Backs Daily Bills **and** Credit Bills — one dataset, two views (FR-RPT-003).

`status` (Canceled Bills, 2026-11-10): omit it for the normal Daily/Credit Bills
behaviour, which now excludes cancelled bills by default; pass `status=cancelled`
for the dedicated Canceled Bills screen.

schema.title: Response List Invoices Api V1 Invoices Get

get.description:
One bill with its lines.

`credit.read` is accepted as well as `reports.sales.read` because this is how the
Credit Bills folder shows what a customer actually bought on an invoice. Every
seeded role holding `credit.read` happens to hold `reports.sales.read` too, so this
changes nothing for them — it stops a *custom* credit-only role from seeing a
customer's bill list it may read and then a 403 on every bill in it.

No widening of what is returned: the cost snapshot still needs `catalog.cost.read`
and is omitted, not nulled (FR-CAT-004), and `InvoiceReader.get` predicates on the
caller's `business_id` so a cross-tenant id is a 404.

schema.title: Response Get Invoice Api V1 Invoices  Invoice Id  Get

get.description:
Everything needed to render the document (FR-PRINT-001).

**A plain read.** It never calls a finalisation endpoint and creates nothing — no
sale, no number, no movement.

schema.title: Response Get Print Payload Api V1 Invoices  Invoice Id  Print Payload Get

post.description:
Records a print attempt (FR-PRINT-004).

A logging failure **never blocks printing**: a customer waiting for their bill is
not a good moment to fail on an audit nicety, so the error is logged server-side and
the route still succeeds.

Reverses stock exactly, issues a full-value credit note for a credit sale,
**retains** the internal reference and keeps the record listed.

schema.title: Response Cancel Invoice Api V1 Invoices  Invoice Id  Cancel Post

post.description:
Edit a finalised bill **in place** (owner Decision A, 2026-11-07).

Keeps the invoice's id and internal reference, writes the complete before-state to
`invoice_revisions`, recomputes the money server-side, reconciles stock with new
append-only movements, and never touches a payment.

`Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retried save applies once rather than writing a
second revision and a second set of stock movements.

Refuses, with its own error code each time: a stale `expected_version`
(`409 INVOICE_VERSION_CONFLICT`), a cancelled bill (`409 INVOICE_NOT_EDITABLE`), and
a new total below what has already been paid (`409 EDIT_BELOW_PAID_TOTAL` — the
owner's explicit rule; the correction there is a return or a credit note).

schema.title: Response Amend Invoice Api V1 Invoices  Invoice Id  Amend Post

get.description: The edit history of one bill, newest first, with each before-state's lines.

schema.title: Response Invoice Revisions Api V1 Invoices  Invoice Id  Revisions Get

get.description:
Counts, gross, discount, tax, net, and a breakdown by payment method.

**Credit sales are included**, on their sale date (FR-RPT-001) — a credit sale is a
sale, and excluding it would understate the day's trading.

schema.title: Response Daily Sales Api V1 Reports Daily Sales Get

get.description:
The other view of the same dataset as `daily-sales`. The two must reconcile
exactly (FR-RPT-003).

schema.title: Response Credit Outstanding Report Api V1 Reports Credit Outstanding Get

get.description:
Proves daily sales and credit outstanding describe the same money.

A `reconciles: false` means `amount_paid` has drifted from the allocations, which is
NFR-DATA-003 failing — it is reported, never auto-corrected.

schema.title: Response Reconciliation Check Api V1 Reports Reconciliation Check Get
Response Stock Position Api V1 Reports Stock Position Get

get.description:
Margin requires `catalog.cost.read` on top of this report's permission; the
columns are **omitted** rather than nulled when it is absent.

schema.title: Response Item Sales Api V1 Reports Item Sales Get

get.description: Cash expected versus collected, per counter per day.

schema.title: Response Counter Reconciliation Api V1 Reports Counter Reconciliation Get

get.description:
Streaming CSV (FR-RPT-007).

Leading `=`, `+`, `-` and `@` are escaped, so a product named `=cmd()` arrives in
the accountant's spreadsheet as text rather than a formula.

post.description:
Apply a bounded batch of safe offline operations.

A bad operation never blocks the rest of the batch, except that operations for the
**same entity** stop at the first failure to preserve ordering — a later edit
applied before an unresolved earlier one would silently reorder the user's work.

schema.title: Response Apply Operations Api V1 Sync Operations Post

get.description:
A bounded delta for the offline cache.

**`cost_price` is never included, regardless of permission** — a stolen counter
machine must not carry the shop's margins (`SECURITY.md §11`).

schema.title: Response Catalog Delta Api V1 Sync Catalog Get

get.description:
One call after login.

Publishes the **money policy** so the client never hardcodes a rounding rule, the
client-visible settings, the print profile and the date order — and states plainly
that offline finalisation is refused, so the client can show the reason rather than
inventing one.

schema.title: Response Bootstrap Api V1 Sync Bootstrap Get

get.description: The registry, so a client can verify it rather than assume it.

schema.title: Response Operation Types Api V1 Sync Operation Types Get
Response List Suppliers Api V1 Suppliers Get
Response Upsert Supplier Api V1 Suppliers  Supplier Id  Put

post.description:
Creates a `draft`. **No stock change** — recording a supplier's delivery note is
not the same as the goods being on the shelf.

schema.title: Response Create Purchase Api V1 Purchases Post
Response List Purchases Api V1 Purchases Get

post.description: **The only path that receives stock** (FR-PUR-003). Idempotent.

schema.title: Response Confirm Purchase Api V1 Purchases  Purchase Id  Confirm Post

post.description:
Only while `draft`. A confirmed receipt is immutable — correcting it is a
supplier return or an adjustment, not an edit.

Credits the **snapshot price** — what the customer paid, not today's price.

Damaged goods, or an explicit `restock: false`, become **scrap** rather than
sellable stock.

schema.title: Response Create Return Api V1 Returns Post
Response List Returns Api V1 Returns Get

post.description:
Accept a file and queue it for parsing (FR-IMP-001/002/003/004).

`202`, not `201`: the job exists but has not been read yet. The client polls
`GET /imports/{id}` for the state machine, which is honest about what has actually
happened — a `201` would imply the rows are ready.

schema.title: Response Upload Import Api V1 Imports Post

get.description:
Import history (FR-IMP-009).

`before` is a job's `ordinal`, not a timestamp. A timestamp cursor over a
non-unique column can skip or repeat a row (migration `0020`).

schema.title: Response List Imports Api V1 Imports Get

get.description: Job status and counts (FR-IMP-005).

schema.title: Response Get Import Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Get

get.description: The review queue (FR-IMP-006).

schema.title: Response Get Import Rows Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Rows Get

patch.description:
Record one human decision (FR-IMP-007).

The body is a plain dict rather than a model because it carries exactly two
optional keys and a strict model here would add a schema for `{decision,
matched_product_id}` that says nothing the enum does not.

schema.title: Response Decide Import Row Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Rows  Row Id  Patch

post.description:
One decision for every pending row in a status.

Not in the original route list, and added for a reason that only shows up with a
real file: a supplier price list of 400 unstocked parts produces 400 `new_product`
rows, and a reviewer forced to click each one will stop reading by row 20. A
decision about a whole category is a judgement someone can actually hold in mind.

schema.title: Response Decide All Import Rows Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Rows Decide All Post

post.description:
Apply the accepted rows in one transaction (FR-IMP-008).

`idempotency_key` is required by the API contract and accepted here; the job's own
terminal `applied` state is what actually prevents a second application, which is
the stronger guarantee — it holds even for a client that generates a fresh key.

schema.title: Response Apply Import Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Apply Post

post.description: Cancel a job that has not been applied (FR-IMP-005).

schema.title: Response Cancel Import Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Cancel Post

get.description:
Per-row outcome, retained for audit (FR-IMP-009).

Returns every row with its result and reason — including the skipped ones, which are
the whole point. "47 applied" without "and these 3 were skipped because the part
code matched nothing" is a report that hides exactly what the reader needs.

schema.title: Response Import Report Api V1 Imports  Job Id  Report Get

get.description:
The caller's business's active notices — Feature A.1/A.2.

No specific permission: these are notices about the business the caller is already
signed in to, and gating "stock has run out" behind a reports permission would mean
the person at the counter is the one person who cannot be told.

schema.title: Response List Notifications Api V1 Notifications Get
Response Mark Notification Read Api V1 Notifications  Notification Id  Read Post

post.description:
"Check later." Stops the reminder; changes nothing it refers to (owner
request, 2026-11-10 — dismissing a low-stock notice must not raise stock).

schema.title: Response Dismiss Notification Api V1 Notifications  Notification Id  Dismiss Post

post.description:
"Seen, and I'm on it." For notifications with no server-verifiable resolution
of their own. Acknowledging a bill reminder must not mark the bill paid.

schema.title: Response Acknowledge Notification Api V1 Notifications  Notification Id  Acknowledge Post
Response Snooze Notification Api V1 Notifications  Notification Id  Snooze Post

get.description:
Whether an operational alert would actually reach anybody (OD-19).

Behind `audit.read` rather than open to any signed-in user: it reports on the
deployment's monitoring posture, which is an operator's concern, and the destination
hint — even reduced to scheme and host — is infrastructure detail a counter hand has
no reason to see.

schema.title: Response Alerting Status Api V1 Notifications Alerting Get
Response List Reminders Api V1 Reminders Get
Response Create Reminder Api V1 Reminders Post
Response Update Reminder Api V1 Reminders  Reminder Id  Put

Response Create Order Api V1 Orders Post

Set or clear the owner's one-time reminder for one order (owner request).

Fires **ahead of** the flat ten-minute nudge once due, and is consumed (cleared)
the instant it fires — see `domain/orders/service.py::nudge_pending`.

schema.title: Response Set Order Reminder Api V1 Orders  Order Id  Reminder Put
Response Complete Order Api V1 Orders  Order Id  Complete Post
Response Discard Order Api V1 Orders  Order Id  Discard Post

get.description:
Authenticated, but needs no specific permission: it reports the server's own
version and time to whoever is signed in.

schema.title: Response Meta Api V1 Meta Get

AlertingStatusOut.title: AlertingStatusOut
AlertingStatusOut.description:
OD-19's gap, made visible.

`state` is `unconfigured` when alerting is on and no destination is set — an
operator reading `/readyz` can see that alerts are being dropped instead of
discovering it during an incident.

AmendHeaderIn.title: AmendHeaderIn
AmendHeaderIn.description:
Header fields an edit may change.

Every field is optional, and **omitting one leaves it alone** — `model_fields_set` is
what distinguishes "not supplied" from "clear it", so sending `null` deliberately
blanks a field while sending nothing keeps it.

AmendOut.title: AmendOut
AmendOut.description:
`POST /invoices/{id}:amend`. The invoice's identity is **unchanged** — there is
deliberately no new invoice id or reference in this response, because an edit does
not create one.

AssignCounterRequest.title: AssignCounterRequest
AssignCounterRequest.description:
`null` detaches the computer from every counter.

A sub-resource carrying one field rather than a general `PUT /admin/devices/{id}`:
this is the only device column an administrator may set here, and a wider body would
let a counter assignment also rewrite a device's label, branch or revocation state.

BootstrapBusinessOut.title: BootstrapBusinessOut
BootstrapBusinessOut.description:
The shop's heading as configured. Every field may be empty, and an empty field is
rendered as nothing — never a placeholder and never the reference workbook's address
(FR-PRINT-016, OD-4).

CatalogDeltaOut.title: CatalogDeltaOut
CatalogDeltaOut.description:
⚠️ `cost_price` is **never** present, regardless of permission: a stolen counter
machine must not carry the shop's margins (`SECURITY.md §11`).

CreditCustomerOut.title: CreditCustomerOut
CreditCustomerOut.description:
Every aggregate is **server-computed**; the client never sums these
(FR-RPT-030, ADR-032).

DailySalesOut.title: DailySalesOut
DailySalesOut.description: `GET /reports/daily-sales` — the one report a screen renders field by field.

DraftPreviewTotalsOut.title: DraftPreviewTotalsOut
DraftPreviewTotalsOut.description:
Always advisory. The server recomputes everything at finalisation
(FR-DRAFT-011).

FinalizeOut.title: FinalizeOut
FinalizeOut.description: The `201` from `POST /sales:finalize` — cash and credit alike (ADR-033).

ImportReportOut.title: ImportReportOut
ImportReportOut.description: FR-IMP-009. Carries the skipped rows and their reasons, not just the counts.

ImportUploadOut.title: ImportUploadOut
ImportUploadOut.description:
`202` from `POST /imports`.

`duplicate_of_job_id` is present and null on a normal upload rather than omitted:
unlike `cost_price`, its absence carries no permission meaning, and a client
checking `=== null` is clearer than one checking `in`.

InvoiceOut.title: InvoiceOut
InvoiceOut.description:
One shape, returned by `POST /sales:finalize` **and** `GET /invoices/{id}`.

Built by a single serialiser (`api/v1/serialize.py`), because the confirmation card
and the Daily Bills detail describe the same bill.

InvoiceRevisionOut.title: InvoiceRevisionOut
InvoiceRevisionOut.description:
One recorded before-state. Immutable: `invoice_revisions` is `SELECT, INSERT`
only at the privilege level.

LifecycleStatusOut.title: LifecycleStatusOut
LifecycleStatusOut.description: The body every dismiss/acknowledge/snooze/read action returns.

MechanicSuggestionOut.title: MechanicSuggestionOut
MechanicSuggestionOut.description: Reference data, so no monetary field appears here at all.

MoneyPolicyOut.title: MoneyPolicyOut
MoneyPolicyOut.description: Published so the client never hardcodes a rounding or whole-rupee rule.

MovementReportLineOut.title: MovementReportLineOut
MovementReportLineOut.description: One movement on the day's report.

PaymentHistoryOut.title: PaymentHistoryOut
PaymentHistoryOut.description:
One row of `GET /payments`.

Declared for M25: the customer screen shows a payment history, and an undeclared
response left the client stringifying `unknown` values — which ESLint correctly
refused, because `String(someObject)` yields `[object Object]` on a screen showing
money.

PrintBusinessOut.title: PrintBusinessOut
PrintBusinessOut.description: Empty optional fields print nothing — **never a placeholder** (FR-PRINT-016).

PrintPayloadOut.title: PrintPayloadOut
PrintPayloadOut.description:
⚠️ Carries **no invoice number** of any kind (OD-3, T3-06).

`document_title` comes from the server only and is `ESTIMATE` for cash and credit
alike until the FR-TAX-003 gate passes (OD-24, FR-PRINT-021).

ReportOut.title: ReportOut
ReportOut.description:
The common report envelope (`API-SPECIFICATION.md §3.11`).

⚠️ The **only** permissive model in this module. Each report spreads its own figures
at the top level — `daily-sales` has `gross`/`net`/`by_day`, `stock-position` has
`rows` — so `extra="forbid"` would make one model impossible. The envelope is what
every report shares and what the client relies on; the per-report figures are typed
where a screen renders them field by field (`DailySalesOut`).

SaleHeaderIn.title: SaleHeaderIn
SaleHeaderIn.description: Optional for **both** sale types, and persisted when present (FR-CREDIT-012).

StockEntryCandidateOut.title: StockEntryCandidateOut
StockEntryCandidateOut.description: One of several products sharing a normalised name, for the user to choose between.

StockEntryMatchOut.title: StockEntryMatchOut
StockEntryMatchOut.description:
What saving this row would do, answered before anything is written.

`kind` is one of:

| `kind` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `new` | No product has this name; saving creates one |
| `existing` | One active product matches; saving **adds** to its stock |
| `ambiguous` | Two or more match — the user must pick, nothing is guessed |
| `inactive` | The match is withdrawn from the catalog; reactivate it first |

StockEntryRow.title: StockEntryRow
StockEntryRow.description: One row of the owner's four-column sheet: Item · Price · Min Qty · Stock Qty.

UnattendedRequest.title: UnattendedRequest
UnattendedRequest.description: No credentials — the device is the only thing the caller supplies.
